Remote support.
Free. Simple. Yours.

Help your parents with their Android phone from your browser. Our free hosted service is coming soon. You can already download the source code and run your own RemotePocket server.

I built RemotePocket to help my parents without asking them to approve every connection after we set it up together.

Getting started

From your account
to your first session.

These steps apply to your own installation and, at launch, to the public service. Use the web app on your computer and the Android app on the phone you want to help with.

  1. 01

    Open the web app

    Create your account or sign in. You can open the app directly from a shared link. For password recovery, add and verify your email address.

  2. 02

    Prepare the phone

    Install the Android app and link the phone to your account using the code from the web app. Choose a password for remote support and follow the app’s instructions to allow the access it needs.

  3. 03

    Send a message

    In the web app, choose “Attiva tramite SMS o Telegram”. Copy the message and send it by SMS or Telegram to the phone you want to help with. The phone connects by itself: the person using it does not need to tap the message.

  4. 04

    Start helping

    When the phone appears online, enter its device password and open a session. View the screen, tap, swipe and type in supported fields.

Set it up together, once

The person using the phone must agree and grant RemotePocket access during setup. They do not need to approve each connection afterwards. To see the screen, you need Android 11 or newer, internet access and an unlocked phone.

If Android closes RemotePocket or the phone locks, the person holding it may need to help. Some apps may prevent you from seeing or controlling their content.

Just send an SMS or Telegram message

Connect when help is needed.

Designed to save battery between support sessions. RemotePocket does not stay connected all day. When help is needed, copy a message from the web app and send it by SMS or Telegram. The phone connects by itself. After support ends, it goes back to waiting.

SMS

To the phone number

Send the message prepared by RemotePocket as an SMS to the phone you want to help with. First, allow RemotePocket to receive SMS in the phone’s settings.

TELEGRAM

In a conversation

Send the same message to the Telegram account used on the phone. A notification must appear with the message text. First, allow RemotePocket to read notifications in the phone’s settings.

USE IT OFTEN?

You can keep it connected

Enable “Mantieni connessione al server” in the Android app. You can then provide support without sending a message each time.

You still need the password to start

RemotePocket prepares the message and you send it. To see the screen and help, enter the password you chose for that phone in RemotePocket into the web app.

The message must arrive within 10 minutes of being created. Once the phone receives it, you have 10 minutes to start. You can then stay connected for as long as you are helping. When you finish, the connection closes after 5 minutes unless you start again.

The phone needs internet access and must be unlocked for you to see the screen. It is normal for it to appear offline while waiting for a message. The person using the phone can pause RemotePocket at any time: messages will not make it connect while paused.

How connections work

Know where
your session goes.

The server connects you

Screen images and commands pass through the RemotePocket server between your browser and the phone.

Choose who runs the server

The hosted service will use a server operated by RemotePocket. With your own installation, you choose and manage the server.

Account and activity data

The server stores accounts, paired devices and activity history to operate the service. With your own installation, the server administrator manages this data.
